🇲🇽🏭 MEXICO'S EXPORT BOOM IS ALSO A WARNING

Mexican electronics and computing exports exploded 95.6% year-on-year in Q1 to $50.078 billion — Chihuahua alone shipped $26 billion, up 119%. But INEGI's own numbers show the trap underneath: 92% of it goes to the United States and 96% is made in just five states. Banco Base's Gabriela Siller lays out three risks stacked on one buyer: "more than 90% of exports go to the United States, 67.25% of those imports go to Texas." The case for diversification writes itself.

🔥🇲🇽 GARCÍA LUNA'S PRISON-LOOTING NETWORK KEEPS FALLING

A federal judge just bound over Jesús Gabriel Pérez Rodríguez for embezzlement and criminal association — another node of Genaro García Luna's machine. The FGR says the ring diverted more than 5 billion pesos meant for federal prison upkeep under the ex-security secretary, laundering 2.95 billion through shell companies and fake invoices tied to the husband of TV host Inés Gómez Mont. Sixty people were charged in the same scheme.

TIME: U.S. Declines to Renew Trade Pact With Mexico and Canada — Here's What It Means
July 2, 2026 | 🟡

"Declines" — passive, tidy, blameless. It was Trump who refused the 16-year extension; the deal now drops into a decade of annual reviews. TIME leads with a "senior U.S. official" citing trade deficits and fear of Chinese firms using Mexico as a backdoor — US grievances first, the Mexican economy left hanging last. 8–13 million US jobs ride on this trade, yet the "uncertainty" is framed as everyone's, not Washington's choice.

Even the reassurance is on US terms: officials call the non-renewal "not a doomsday scenario" while pocketing the leverage of yearly reviews.

• a "senior U.S. official" wants to fix "shortcomings" like dairy and corn market access
• "not a doomsday scenario"

CNN: Mexico's human trafficking survivors have a message for World Cup fans
June 30, 2026 | 🟡

CNN routes "a message for World Cup fans" through human trafficking survivors — dropped the same week Mexico was center-stage on the pitch. The survivors are real and worth hearing; the timing turns Mexico's biggest sports moment into a warning label. Rarely mentioned: the US is the largest consumer market driving the demand behind that trade.

The 140,000+ officially disappeared are a genuine crisis Mexican mothers march over year-round — but US coverage reaches for it precisely when Mexico steps onto a global stage.

NYT (opinion, Ioan Grillo): Mexico's World Cup Moment Is Pure, Fragile Magic
July 5, 2026 | 🟢

Even the NYT let the joy stand. Ioan Grillo, 25 years in CDMX: "I had never witnessed the level of euphoria this tournament has unleashed." Barrios crowding around street-stall TVs. The rare piece with no cartel disclaimer bolted onto the headline.

The "fragile" nods to real pain — homicides, disappearances — but Grillo reports the celebration as legitimate, not a distraction to be scolded.

• "In my quarter-century living in Mexico City, I had never witnessed the level of euphoria this tournament has unleashed."
• "We needed something emotional, to unite us." — Yanira Córdoba

🇲🇽💵 REMITTANCES RISE A FOURTH STRAIGHT MONTH — TRUMP'S CRACKDOWN ISN'T LANDING

Banco de México reports migrants sent home $5,611 million dollars in May, up 3.8% year-on-year and the fourth consecutive month of growth. And it comes after Trump's decree ordering US banks to investigate migrant money transfers. The lifeline Mexicans abroad send to their families didn't shrink under pressure — it kept climbing.

🇲🇽🚺 THE PENSION NEOLIBERALISM NEVER PAID: WOMEN'S UNPAID CARE WORK

In Quiroga, Michoacán, Sheinbaum handed out cards for the Women's Welfare Pension — a benefit that recognizes the unpaid care work of women aged 60 to 64, a lifetime of labor the market never counted. "Las mujeres somos el alma de la nación," she said, presenting it alongside a LIBRE Center for women in every municipality and the Women's Rights Charter against machismo. She didn't arrive alone to the presidency.

🚨🇲🇽 SHEINBAUM TO WASHINGTON: SHOW THE EVIDENCE

The US Treasury publicly accused fuel-smuggling networks tied to the CJNG of financing Mexican political campaigns — without ever showing Mexico a shred of proof first. Sheinbaum's answer: "De las campañas nunca fuimos informados. ¿Qué pruebas tienen?" Mexico's own financial-intelligence unit (UIF) was already investigating those same individuals — and Washington itself demands hard evidence for every extradition request Mexico submits.

🇲🇽🛢️ SEMARNAT RULES OUT CAMPECHE "OIL SPILL" AFTER FISHERMEN'S ALERT

When Campeche fishermen reported an oil slick four nautical miles off Lerma, Mexico's environmental authorities moved the same day. Semarnat, Pemex, Profepa, the energy-safety agency ASEA and the Navy ran a physical inspection, and the Campeche Hydrocarbon Committee confirmed no presence of hydrocarbons on the coast. Alert raised July 5, verified and cleared by July 6.

🇲🇽🏭 GUANAJUATO'S EXPORTS TO ENGLAND JUMPED 194%

As Mexico faced England at the Azteca, Guanajuato was already winning off the pitch: exports to England surged 193.9% in Q1 to over $10.5 million — cars, auto parts, and Mexican condiments. 47 firms, 30,587 families employed. Silao alone up 374%.
